content:
Apple will launch several brand-new Mac products later this year, including the first MacBook with a touchscreen and the first models equipped with the M6 chip. Below is all the information we currently have about the upcoming new Macs.

MacBook Ultra

The flagship Mac launching later this year will be Apple's first Mac to feature a touchscreen. Whether this new machine will ultimately be named MacBook Pro or MacBook Ultra remains to be seen, but it will represent the most significant design overhaul of the MacBook Pro in years.

Reports indicate that Apple is testing a high-end MacBook model with macOS 27.1, with the system expected to be officially released at the end of October.

This new MacBook will be Apple's first laptop to feature both a touchscreen and an OLED display. The device is also expected to drop the notch design in favour of a Dynamic Island-style design similar to the iPhone. Bloomberg has also reported that the new high-end MacBook will be thinner than the current MacBook Pro.

In terms of performance, the new touchscreen MacBook will use the same M5 Pro and M5 Max chips as the current MacBook Pro.

M6 MacBook

Apple is reportedly planning to launch its first Mac with the M6 chip later this year, and is currently developing an updated entry-level MacBook Pro equipped with the next-generation M6 processor.

Reports suggest that the M6 will offer faster memory bandwidth and improvements in both CPU and GPU core performance.

Aside from the M6 chip, the new entry-level MacBook Pro is not expected to feature any other major changes.

iMac

Apple last updated the 24-inch iMac in October 2024, upgrading the chip from M3 to M4. Apple is now developing the next-generation iMac update, which is reportedly slated for release this autumn.

The new iMac is expected to feature Apple's upcoming M6 chip. There are also rumours that the new iMac will be available in a range of new colour options.

Mac mini and Mac Studio (Possibly)

Lastly, Apple is also developing updated versions of the Mac mini and Mac Studio, though release dates remain unclear.

Reports indicate that Apple is testing a new Mac mini lineup featuring M5 Pro and entry-level M6 chips, while the Mac Studio is being tested with M5 Max and M5 Ultra processors.

Bloomberg noted that the release dates for these models remain uncertain, depending on the "supply situation of memory chips." The market had previously widely expected the new Mac Studio to launch by year-end, but this now appears to be in doubt.

The current Mac mini is available with M4 and M4 Pro chips, while the Mac Studio comes in M4 Max and M3 Ultra configurations.

Summary

Affected by memory and storage supply constraints across the industry, Apple's Mac lineup is currently in a slightly awkward stage. However, the company still has a fairly strong lineup of new machines ready to go. What are your thoughts on the new Macs launching by year-end? And how much do you think the MacBook Ultra will cost? Feel free to let us know in the comments section.
